title: Continents drift about as fast as your fingernails grow
body: Earth’s rigid outer shell is broken into tectonic plates that glide over the hot, slowly deforming mantle beneath. At the Mid-Atlantic Ridge they spread apart by roughly 1 to 4 cm a year, about fingernail speed, while the Pacific’s Nazca Plate moves up to about 16 cm a year. Tiny as that sounds, over roughly 200 million years such motion tore apart the supercontinent Pangaea and opened the whole Atlantic Ocean.

slides.question: How far does the Pacific’s Nazca Plate move in a year, at most?
slides.explanation: Up to about 16 cm a year, against roughly 1 to 4 cm at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. Over about 200 million years, such motion tore Pangaea apart and opened the Atlantic.
